sections.title: Finniss: Resource, Reserve & Production
sections.subtitle: Lithium-specific drivers -- updated on drilling/reserve releases, not every period

charts.title: Finniss Mineral Resource & Ore Reserve
charts.annotation: JORC Resource/Reserve estimates are only restated when new drilling is released, so this is a step series, not an annual one. The FY2026 annual report cites a further-updated 15.6Mt Ore Reserve across Grants, BP33 and Carlton (33% tonnage increase) not yet captured as a dated data point here.

charts.title: Spodumene Concentrate Produced
charts.annotation: FY2023 is Finniss's only full year of production before the 2024 price-crash suspension. Mining restarted at the Grants open pit in May 2026, first new concentrate was produced in September 2026, and first shipment of new-production spodumene is targeted for the December-2026 quarter -- the tonnes that validate the restart are not yet in this series.

charts.title: Exploration Spend
charts.annotation: Covers Finniss resource-definition drilling and the Blackbeard lithium prospect; spend was cut sharply through the 2024-2026 care-and-maintenance period and is not separately broken out in every filing.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Core Lithium Ltd: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Core Lithium Ltd: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Core Lithium Ltd: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Core Lithium Ltd: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Core Lithium Ltd: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Core Lithium Ltd: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Core Lithium Ltd: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

resourceReserve.title: Mineral Resource and Ore Reserve
resourceReserve.content:
The Mineral Resource is the JORC-code estimate of mineralisation with reasonable prospects of eventual economic extraction; the Ore Reserve is the smaller, economically-mineable subset under a current mine plan. Grade is lithium oxide content (Li2O%).

For Core Lithium: Finniss's Ore Reserve (Grants, BP33, Carlton) is what the 20-year mine life and 1.2Mtpa steady-state plan behind the DCF are built from. Growth here comes from drilling converting Resource into mineable Reserve, not from a sales or production metric.

What to watch:

  • Reserve tonnes and grade rising faster than depletion from mining
  • Grade dilution as lower-grade satellite deposits (BP33, Carlton) are added for scale
  • Blackbeard and the newly acquired Bynoe tenement converting exploration into disclosed Resource

spodumeneProduction.title: Spodumene concentrate produced
spodumeneProduction.content:
Tonnes of spodumene (lithium) concentrate physically produced at the Finniss DMS plant in the period, before shipment or sale.

For Core Lithium: Finniss produced for roughly a year in FY2023 before the 2024 lithium-price crash forced an 18-month suspension. The FY2026 restart -- FID in March 2026, first concentrate in September 2026 -- is the entire investment case, so this is the series that will show whether the ramp toward the 214ktpa (scaling to 1.2Mtpa with BP33 underground) nameplate is actually happening once new tonnes are reported.

What to watch:

  • Tonnes produced against the 214ktpa nameplate, then the 1.2Mtpa BP33 steady state
  • The gap between tonnes produced and tonnes shipped (stockpile build or drawdown)
  • Unit cost per tonne falling as throughput ramps

explorationSpend.title: Exploration spend
explorationSpend.content:
Cash spent on resource-definition and greenfield drilling, expensed or capitalised depending on the project's stage.

For Core Lithium: this spend funds the Resource/Reserve growth above and the Blackbeard lithium target and Bynoe tenement that sit outside the current 1.2Mtpa mine plan -- the exploration upside beyond Finniss's reserve base.

What to watch:

  • Spend resuming now the restart is funded, after being cut hard during care-and-maintenance
  • Drilling results converting into Resource/Reserve upgrades within a year or two

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Core Lithium Ltd: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Core Lithium Ltd: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
